questions.title: Section A – Multiple Choice, Terms, Matching & Diagrams

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT for oogenesis in humans?

A One diploid mature ovum is formed
B One haploid mature ovum is formed
C Four diploid mature ova are formed
D Four haploid mature ova are formed

options.A: One diploid mature ovum is formed
options.B: One haploid mature ovum is formed
options.C: Four diploid mature ova are formed
options.D: Four haploid mature ova are formed

subQuestions.questionText:
A structure in the eye that contains a high concentration of blood vessels and provides oxygen and nutrients to the retina is the …

A sclera.
B choroid.
C conjunctiva.
D lens.

The vagina …

A transports urine to the outside.
B is the place where the foetus develops.
C produces progesterone.
D acts as a birth canal.

options.B: is the place where the foetus develops.

subQuestions.questionText:
The list below gives the characteristics of some young birds immediately after hatching.

(i) Eyes are open
(ii) Can move around
(iii) Cannot feed themselves
(iv) No feathers

Which ONE of the following combinations represents the characteristics of precocial development?

A (ii) and (iii) only
B (iii) and (iv) only
C (i) and (ii) only
D (ii) and (iv) only

The cornea and the lens are both …

A opaque.
B transparent.
C elastic.
D inelastic.

Which ONE of the following is TRUE for a person who has an underactive thyroid gland?

The TSH levels will be …

A high and the metabolic rate low.
B high and the metabolic rate high.
C low and the metabolic rate low.
D low and the metabolic rate high.

options.A: high and the metabolic rate low.
options.B: high and the metabolic rate high.
options.C: low and the metabolic rate low.
options.D: low and the metabolic rate high.

A Glasses with biconvex lenses

Description: The plant hormone that stimulates the germination of seeds.
A: Gibberellins

questions.title: Brain, Male Reproductive System, Ovovivipary, ADH & Plant Defence

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows part of the human brain (with hypothalamus labelled and parts A, B, C, D). Identify part A.
State TWO functions of part D (cerebrum).
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: Higher thought processes / intelligence / memory / reasoning; Interpretation of all senses; Controls all voluntary actions. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the hormone secreted by gland C (pituitary) that has an effect on long bones.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the hormone secreted by gland C (pituitary) that has an effect on mammary glands in the breasts.
State ONE way in which the brain is protected.
Describe the role of the hypothalamus in thermoregulation.
subQuestions.memoText: It receives / interprets impulses from receptors in the skin and sends impulses to the blood vessels of the skin / influences blood flow to the skin and the sweat glands / influences sweat secretion.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.6(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Part B (medulla oblongata) is involved in the homeostatic control of the carbon dioxide concentration in the blood. State the location of the receptors that are stimulated by an increase in the carbon dioxide concentration in the blood.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.6(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the TWO effectors that part B (medulla oblongata) sends impulses to.
subQuestions.memoText: Heart muscle; Diaphragm / Intercostal muscles / Breathing muscles. (Mark first TWO only.)

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows part of the male reproductive system (parts A, B, C with A cut and tied). Identify part A.
State ONE function of part B (epididymis).
subQuestions.memoText: Sperm storage / Sperm maturation (Mark first ONE only)

subQuestions.questionText: During a vasectomy, part A (vas deferens) is cut and tied as shown in the diagram. Semen will still be released during copulation. Explain the composition of the semen after a vasectomy.
subQuestions.memoText: The semen will not contain sperm because they are not transported, but will contain all other secretions of the accessory glands / examples thereof; the vasectomy occurred before the accessory glands. (Any 3)

subQuestions.questionText: In some rare cases, males are born with part C (testis) located inside the body because it failed to descend into the scrotum. Explain how this condition may affect male fertility.
subQuestions.memoText: The temperature of the testes inside the body will be too high; no / abnormal sperm will be produced; the man will be infertile / not able to reproduce.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process of spermatogenesis.
subQuestions.memoText: Under the influence of testosterone, diploid cells / germinal epithelial cells in the seminiferous tubules / testes undergo meiosis to form haploid sperm cells. (Any 4)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the developing embryo is protected and nourished in ovoviviparous organisms.
subQuestions.memoText: Protection (compulsory 1* + any 4): The (amniotic) egg is retained inside the mother's body* to protect the embryo from predators; the allantois protects the embryo by removing waste products; the embryo is protected from shocks / sudden changes in temperature / dehydration by the chorion, amnion, amniotic fluid inside the amniotic membrane, shell / outer covering, air pocket. Nourishment (any 2): The embryo receives nutrients from the egg yolk in the yolk sac and from the albumen. (Max 5 protection + 2 nourishment = 7)

subQuestions.questionText: An investigation was conducted to determine the change in ADH levels in the blood and the volume of urine produced over a 24-hour period. Graph A shows average ADH levels in the blood (15:00 = 2,06 pg/dℓ; 03:00 = 4,7 pg/dℓ) and Graph B shows average urine volume (08:00–20:00 = 71,53 mℓ/h; 20:00–08:00 = 34,72 mℓ/h). Calculate the difference between the average volume of urine (mℓ/h) produced during the 2 time periods. Show ALL workings.
Explain how the ADH levels in the blood at 03:00 affects the volume of urine produced between 20:00 and 08:00.
subQuestions.memoText: The high level of ADH at night increases the permeability of the renal tubules / collecting duct / distal convoluted tubules in the kidney; more water is reabsorbed / less water is excreted; less urine is produced.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE advantage of the high ADH levels at 03:00.
subQuestions.memoText: Less urine produced / more water is retained; a person will not need to urinate often / will not be thirsty / sleep will not be interrupted.

subQuestions.questionText: A patient whose renal tubules are impermeable to water underwent the same investigation. Explain why the ADH levels are expected to remain high all the time.
subQuestions.memoText: Water will not be reabsorbed from the renal tubules; the volume of water in the blood will be low; the pituitary gland will be stimulated to release more ADH all the time. (Any 3)

subQuestions.questionText: Some plants contain chemical substances such as alkaloids and cyanogenic glycosides. Caffeine is an example of an alkaloid that occurs in plants like Coffea arabica, Camelia sinensis and Theobroma cacao. Nicotine is another alkaloid found in tobacco plants. Name TWO alkaloids that are found in plants.
Explain TWO ways in which caffeine production acts as a defence mechanism in plants.
subQuestions.memoText: The bitter taste will prevent herbivores from feeding on them; the caffeine will kill pathogenic fungi, protecting the plants from disease / death. (Any 2 x 2; Mark first TWO only)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE other plant defence mechanism.

questions.title: Phototropism, FSH Investigation, Placenta, Ear & Diabetes Mellitus

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the role of auxins in phototropism when a plant is exposed to unilateral light.
subQuestions.memoText: Auxins move away from light; there is a higher concentration of auxins on the dark side of the stem; growth is stimulated on the dark side which grows faster, causing the stem to grow / bend towards the light.

subQuestions.questionText: An investigation was conducted to compare the average FSH levels in 4 different age groups of females (20–32: 7,0; 33–35: 7,8; 36–40: 8,0; 41–50: 8,5). State TWO factors, regarding the females, that should have been kept constant during the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any two of: Must have regular menstrual cycles; They must not become pregnant; Diet. (Mark first TWO only)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways in which the reliability of the results was ensured.
subQuestions.memoText: 250 females per group were used / 1000 females participated; Measurement was done for 5 cycles. (Mark first TWO only)

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE conclusion that can be drawn from the results.
subQuestions.memoText: Older groups of women have a higher (average) FSH level than the younger groups. OR Younger groups of women have a lower (average) FSH level than the older groups. (Mark first ONE only)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the oestrogen levels may remain low in the blood of the females in the 41–50 age group.
subQuestions.memoText: The Graafian / developing follicles secrete oestrogen; but since the number of follicles are low / depleted, less / no oestrogen will be secreted.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why females that were using progesterone-based pills were excluded from the investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: A high concentration of progesterone inhibits the pituitary gland / results in reduced FSH secretion; this will decrease the validity of the investigation. (Any 3)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the development of the placenta and umbilical cord from the time of implantation.
subQuestions.memoText: After implantation the chorion develops many finger-like outgrowths called chorionic villi; the endometrium together with the chorionic villi forms the placenta; the umbilical artery and the umbilical vein develop inside a hollow tube to form the umbilical cord between the foetus and the placenta. (Any 6)

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The diagram represents part of the human ear with a middle-ear infection (parts A, B, C, D, E, F with fluid filled area). Identify part B.

subQuestions.label: 3.4.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify part D in the human ear diagram.
State ONE function of part A (pinna).
subQuestions.memoText: Collects the sound waves / Directs the sound waves towards the auditory canal. (Mark first ONE only)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how middle-ear infection could affect hearing.
subQuestions.memoText: Part D / the ossicles do not vibrate freely; fewer / no vibrations will be sent to the oval window / inner ear; fewer / no pressure waves will be set up in the cochlea; the receptors / organ of Corti will be stimulated less / not stimulated; the cerebrum is stimulated differently / not stimulated; which leads to hearing loss. (Any 4)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the role of the Eustachian tube.
subQuestions.memoText: It equalises pressure on either side of the tympanic membrane.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the small device that is used in the treatment of middle-ear infection.
Write down the LETTER of the part where the small device, named in QUESTION 3.4.5, is inserted.
Describe how part E (semicircular canals) is involved in maintaining balance when there is a change in the speed and direction of movement of the head.
subQuestions.memoText: The cristae are stimulated to convert the stimuli to impulses; the impulses are sent to the cerebellum where they are interpreted; the cerebellum sends impulses to the skeletal muscles to maintain balance. (Any 4)

subQuestions.questionText: Type I diabetes mellitus is caused by pancreatic cells which cannot produce insulin. In type II diabetes mellitus the pancreas does secrete insulin, but the body cells are resistant to the effect of insulin. Name the cells in the pancreas that secrete insulin.

subQuestions.label: 3.5.2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain which type (I or II) of diabetes mellitus would be indicated by the presence of GAD antibodies in the blood.
subQuestions.memoText: Type I; no insulin will be produced; the presence of GAD antibodies indicates that pancreas cells are being destroyed.

subQuestions.label: 3.5.2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain which type (I or II) of diabetes mellitus would be indicated by C-peptide levels at below 0,3 ng/mℓ.
subQuestions.memoText: Type I; a lower than normal C-peptide level indicates that the insulin-producing cells of the pancreas were destroyed; therefore no insulin will be produced.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the insulin levels in the blood of a type II diabetic 2 hours after drinking the glucose solution.
subQuestions.memoText: The insulin levels will remain high because the blood glucose levels remain high; the pancreas will continue secreting insulin.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why a person with untreated diabetes mellitus is expected to be tired all the time.
subQuestions.memoText: The glucose cannot be absorbed into the cells; therefore it cannot be used in cellular respiration / to release energy.
